questions.question_text: An important risk factor for depression and rapid cycling in bipolar disorder is
questions.explanation: Subclinical hypothyroidism is a risk factor for depression and rapid cycling in bipolar disorder.

questions.question_text: The male: female ratio of hypothyroidism is
questions.explanation: Hypothyroidism is more common in women than in men (in the UK, female:male ratio of 6:1).

questions.question_text: Hoover's test is a type of physical examination done to identify the possible diagnosis of
questions.explanation: Hoover's test is useful to identify patients with conversion disorder.

questions.question_text: The clinical feature that is most suggestive of herpes simplex encephalitis is
questions.explanation: Herpes simplex encephalitis: Fairly abrupt onset of confusion, memory impairment, and often seizures.

questions.question_text: A woman who has had Herpes encephalitis develops severe carbohydrate craving, weight gain and inappropriate sexuality. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Herpes simplex encephalitis: HSE is the most common cause of Kluver Bucy syndrome in humans.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about Meige's syndrome is incorrect?

options.text: The patients are more likely to be middle -aged men than women
Oral facial dystonia characterized by repetitive blinking and chin thrusting
The movement is present both at rest and when active

correct_answer.text: The patients are more likely to be middle -aged men than women

correct_answers.text: The patients are more likely to be middle -aged men than women

questions.explanation: The patients are more likely to be women than men and usually at middle age.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a weak inhibitor of cytochrome P450 enzyme system?
questions.explanation: Citalopram is a weak inhibitor.

questions.question_text: Some patients intentionally falsify their symptoms and past history and fabricate signs of physical or mental disorder with the primary aim of obtaining medical attention and treatment. Which of the following diagnosis is most appropriate in these circumstances?
questions.explanation: Factitious disorder (Munchausen's Syndrome): In factitious disorder patients intentionally falsify their symptoms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a risk factor associated with depression in Parkinson's disease?
questions.explanation: Risk factors include Female sex, younger onset, prominent right -sided signs, bradykinesia and gait disturbance.

questions.question_text: All are true about delirium in palliative care except

options.text: Occurs in over 50% of patients at some stage in their illness

questions.explanation: Though small dose of haloperidol or lorazepam is frequently used, they are not always successful in controlling the symptoms.

questions.question_text: Poor prognostic factors with respect to psychiatric morbidity following head injury include all except

options.text: Long period of post traumatic amnesia
Focal damage restricted to the non -dominant lobe
Long duration of loss of consciousness

correct_answer.text: Focal damage restricted to the non -dominant lobe

correct_answers.text: Focal damage restricted to the non -dominant lobe

questions.explanation: Focal non -dominant lobe damage does not indicate poor prognosis.

questions.question_text: Mr.Y suffers from psychiatric symptoms such as apathy, anhedonia, fatigue, and depressed mood. He reports repeated vomiting. On examination you discover unexplained dark skin pigmentation. This should suggest
questions.explanation: Addison's disease: (Cortisol depletion) Psychiatric symptoms - apathy, anhedonia, fatigue, and depressed mood.

questions.question_text: A proportion of patients who are at a high risk of HIV are seronegative but remain anxious about contracting HIV. Which of the following descriptions/diagnosis suits them best?
questions.explanation: The term 'worried well' refers to someone who harbours a fear that he or she has the disease or may contract the infection imminently.

questions.question_text: Depression is thought to be the most common mental illness in those with HIV infection. Which of the following is least likely to explain the high rates of depression noted in HIV -infected individuals?

options.text: Spuriously high diagnosis due to shared symptomatology
Shared risk factors in the two groups

questions.explanation: Antiretroviral therapy is not a common cause of depression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following medications has the best evidence for use in HIV dementia complex?
questions.explanation: Patients with HIV dementia may stabilize or improve slightly on antiretroviral therapy (zidovudine has the best evidence in this regard).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a primary organic disorder due to HIV infection?
questions.explanation: Neuropsychiatric disorders in HIV can be either primary organic (directly due to viral CNS damage) e.g. HIV dementia.

questions.question_text: The most frequent cause of psychiatric hospitalisation in those with HIV seropositivity is
questions.explanation: HIV seems to increase the risk of manic episodes, and mania is the most frequent reason for psychiatric hospitalization.

questions.question_text: A 34 year old homosexual man presents with forgetfulness, loss of concentration, mental slowing. He admits to unsafe sexual practices. He appears clumsy and apathetic. Which of the following statements is false with regard to his diagnosis?

options.text: Decline in memory may not be severe enough to impair all ADLs
Aphasia, agnosia and apraxia are unusual
The minimum duration of symptoms must be 1 year to make the diagnosis
Laboratory evidence of HIV infection is necessary to make the diagnosis
Decline in motor function may be present

correct_answer.text: The minimum duration of symptoms must be 1 year to make the diagnosis

correct_answers.text: The minimum duration of symptoms must be 1 year to make the diagnosis

questions.explanation: Dementia is noted concurrently with initial AIDS -defining illness in 3% of cases. 1 -month duration is sufficient.

questions.question_text: The most common neuropsychiatric symptom associated with Parkinson's disease is
questions.explanation: Depression in PD is very frequent (50%) and is more common in women and in left -sided disease.

questions.question_text: In patients with transient global amnesia, the amnesic episode usually resolves within
questions.explanation: Transient global amnesia episodes last from 6 to 24 hours.

questions.question_text: Which of the following treatments for MS is most likely to lead to depression?
questions.explanation: Among the various interferons, it is Interferon alpha which is clearly associated with depression.

questions.question_text: In post -stroke depression, the antidepressant treatment should be continued for at least
questions.explanation: If there is a good response, antidepressants should be continued for at least 6 months.

questions.question_text: What is the mean duration of a major depressive episode that follows a stroke?
questions.explanation: The mean duration of post-stroke, major depression is 34 weeks.

questions.question_text: A 42 -year-old woman presents with a history of 2 episodes of unilateral blindness that lasted for few weeks. Now she has paraesthesia of left leg and appears quite depressed. Her MRI brain shows multiple demyelinating plaques. With respect to her depression which of the following is NOT correct?

options.text: Can be treated with cognitive behavioural therapy
Has a lifetime prevalence of up to 50% in those with the same neurological condition
Can be caused by the drugs used to treat the neurological condition

questions.explanation: A 20% risk of triggering a relapse of multiple sclerosis has been reported if ECT is given.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following cognitive faculties remains intact in amnestic disorders?
questions.explanation: In amnesic disorders, short-term and recent memory is usually impaired.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true concerning cognitive impairment seen in multiple sclerosis?

options.text: Is best screened for using the Mini -Mental State Examination
Can be explained by the increased prevalence of depression in multiple sclerosis
Has the same feature as a subcortical dementia
Is no more common than in the general population

correct_answer.text: Has the same feature as a subcortical dementia

correct_answers.text: Has the same feature as a subcortical dementia

questions.explanation: Subcortical dementia is a clinical syndrome characterized by slowness of mental processing, forgetfulness, impaired cognition, apathy, and depression.

questions.question_text: With respect to management of Parkinson's disease which of the following is correct?

options.text: Dementia can be treated with any Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors as RCT evidence is abundant
Psychosis is associated with decreases in antiparkinsonian medications
Clozapine must be avoided in Parkinsons psychosis
Quetiapine is best avoided among all antipsychotics
Hypomania is a side effect of levodopa

correct_answer.text: Hypomania is a side effect of levodopa

correct_answers.text: Hypomania is a side effect of levodopa

questions.explanation: Hypomania in Parkinson's disease is mainly drug related.

questions.question_text: The frequency of depressive symptoms in epilepsy is
questions.explanation: Depression - 30-50%, Panic disorder - 20%, Psychosis - 3-7%.

questions.question_text: A 42 -year-old man suffering from poorly controlled epilepsy is referred by the neurologist as non -epileptic seizures are suspected. Which of the following statement is correct?

options.text: Known epileptic patients do not have dissociative seizures
Prolactin levels are elevated after non -epileptic attack
Video recording of ictal and periictal behaviour can help in diagnosis
Presence of depression suggests non -epileptic attacks in most epileptics.
Non epileptic seizures are more common in males

correct_answer.text: Video recording of ictal and periictal behaviour can help in diagnosis

correct_answers.text: Video recording of ictal and periictal behaviour can help in diagnosis

questions.explanation: Video recording along with EEG is the best diagnostic measure.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following drugs is particularly epileptogenic and should be used with caution in epileptic psychosis?
questions.explanation: Clozapine can worsen epileptic psychosis by lowering seizure threshold.

questions.question_text: Post-traumatic epilepsy is seen in what proportion of patients with open head injury?
questions.explanation: Post-traumatic epilepsy is seen in 30% open head injuries (usually during first year) and worsens prognosis.

questions.question_text: Post-concussional syndrome is characterized by all except;
questions.explanation: Post-concussional syndrome is characterized by headache, dizziness, fatigue, poor memory, poor concentration, irritability, depression, sleep disturbance.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is false about mania seen in multiple sclerosis?

options.text: Predominant frontal distribution of plaques in MRI
Is more common than in the general population
Can be induced by prescribed treatments for multiple sclerosis
Can occur as part of the primary physical disorder.

correct_answer.text: Predominant frontal distribution of plaques in MRI

correct_answers.text: Predominant frontal distribution of plaques in MRI

questions.explanation: There is MRI evidence suggesting that patients showing mania with psychotic symptoms have plaques that are distributed predominantly in the bilateral temporal horn areas.

questions.question_text: A 45 -year-old gentleman was admitted to the medical unit with history of stroke. A psychiatric opinion was requested due to his deteriorating mental state. His MRI brain scan showed lesions proximal to the left frontal lobe. Which one of the following psychiatric conditions is most likely to occur in this scenario?
questions.explanation: According to a meta -analytic study the proximity of the lesions to the left frontal lobe predicts depressive illness.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about mania in multiple sclerosis is incorrect?

options.text: There is MRI evidence suggesting that patients showing mania with psychotic symptoms have plaques that are distributed predominantly in the bilateral temporal horn areas
Mild to moderate degrees of mania seen in up to 2/3rd of patients given steroids.
Higher than expected prevalence of mania
People with multiple sclerosis who become hypomanic on steroid therapy are more likely to have a family history of affective disorder.

correct_answer.text: Mild to moderate degrees of mania seen in up to 2/3rd of patients given steroids.

correct_answers.text: Mild to moderate degrees of mania seen in up to 2/3rd of patients given steroids.

questions.explanation: Mild to moderate degrees of mania seen in up to 1/3rd of patients given steroids.

questions.question_text: A psychiatric trainee is keen to obtain prolactin concentrations from a patient to determine possibility of a true seizure activity. What is the time limit after a seizure within which the measurements must be taken?
questions.explanation: Measurements must be taken within 15 min of the event.

questions.question_text: What is the lifetime prevalence of depressive symptoms in patients with multiple sclerosis?
questions.explanation: In patients with multiple sclerosis, lifetime prevalence of depressive symptoms is reported in 40-50%.

questions.question_text: A 65 -year-old gentleman with Parkinson's disease presented with psychotic symptoms characterized by paranoia and visual hallucinations. His wife does not want his antiparkinsonian medication to be stopped as it has worsened the motor features of Parkinsons disease in the past. Which antipsychotic can improve his symptoms without worsening Parkinsonism?
questions.explanation: There is good evidence that low dose clozapine (less than 100 mg/day) can improve psychosis without worsening parkinsonism.

questions.question_text: The gene for Huntington's disease (HD) is located on which chromosome?
questions.explanation: The gene for Huntington's disease (HD) is located on the short arm of chromosome four.

questions.question_text: Head injury may predispose to the development of
questions.explanation: Head injuries, particularly in men, may predispose to the development of Alzheimer's disease.

questions.question_text: Mr. Y has a history of epileptic psychosis and remains psychotic. The most appropriate drug of choice is;
questions.explanation: Drug -induced low mood is an important differential diagnosis.

questions.question_text: The psychiatric syndrome most commonly associated with stroke is
questions.explanation: Depressive illness after stroke is extremely common, occurring in up to 50 -60% of cases.

questions.question_text: Mrs. Z has a history of epilepsy and has now been diagnosed with depression. Which class of drugs should be used as first line treatment in her case?
questions.explanation: SSRIs are the first line; may reduce seizure threshold but rare.

questions.question_text: Lesions caused by an injury to which part of the brain predicts depression?
questions.explanation: Meta -analysis shows that proximity of lesion to left frontal lobe predicts depression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a risk factor associated with cognitive impairment in Parkinson's disease?
questions.explanation: Risk factors are Older patients, late -onset Parkinson's disease , low socio -economic status, low education.

questions.question_text: Concerning movement disorders in Parkinson's disease all are true except

options.text: They may be aggravated by psychotropic medication
Presence of cognitive impairment improves prognosis
Levodopa causes dose dependent psychiatric manifestations

correct_answer.text: Presence of cognitive impairment improves prognosis

correct_answers.text: Presence of cognitive impairment improves prognosis

questions.explanation: The correct answer indicates that cognitive impairments present serious complications for patients in the management of their everyday lives.

questions.question_text: Huntington's disease is transmitted through which of the following genetic changes?

options.text: Autosomal dominant gene on the short arm of chromosome 4
Autosomal dominant gene on the long arm of chromosome 4
Autosomal recessive gene on the short arm of chromosome 4
X-linked recessive gene on the short arm of chromosome 4
Autosomal recessive gene on the short arm of chromosome 4

correct_answer.text: Autosomal dominant gene on the short arm of chromosome 4

correct_answers.text: Autosomal dominant gene on the short arm of chromosome 4

questions.explanation: A single autosomal dominant gene on the short arm of chromosome 4 transmits Huntington's disease.

questions.question_text: During pregnancy, where continued use of Valproate is deemed essential, what is the maximum dose recommended?
questions.explanation: NICE recommends that the dose of Valproate should be limited to 1000 mg a day.

questions.question_text: When used as mood stabilizers, what is the minimum period suggested to withdraw anticonvulsant drugs?
questions.explanation: A period of at least 1 month is suggested.

questions.question_text: What is the lifetime risk of suicide in Huntington's disease?
questions.explanation: The suicide rate for patients with Huntington's disease is higher than that for the general population.

questions.question_text: What is the most common behavioural change observed in patients with Huntington's disease?
questions.explanation: The most common behavioral change observed in patients with Huntington's disease is lack of initiative.

questions.question_text: Which of the following feature is associated more with Huntington's rather than Alzheimer's dementia?

options.text: Impairment in executive function correlates with general cognitive decline

questions.explanation: Sub cortical type of dementia is seen in Huntington's and cortical type is seen in Alzheimer's type.

questions.question_text: Choose an accurate statement with regard to depressive disorders in terminal illness

options.text: It does not respond to antidepressants
Presence of somatic symptoms strongly favour the diagnosis
Depression is uncommon in palliative care settings

questions.explanation: SSRIs do not have much evidence but are widely used in depressed patients receiving palliative care.

questions.question_text: Which of the following tests would be required to make a diagnosis of Huntington's disease in a patient without a family history?
questions.explanation: Sporadic appearance of new mutations is not uncommon in the Huntington disease gene.

questions.question_text: Mr. P has treatment resistant schizophrenia and is currently on clozapine 600 mg /day. Which anticonvulsant should be used to prevent clozapine induced seizures?
questions.explanation: Sodium Valproate is the anticonvulsant of choice as it has a lower incidence of leucopenia than carbamazepine.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about periodic limb movement disorders (PLMD) is incorrect?

options.text: PLMS are a common phenomenon in otherwise healthy individuals.
Its diagnosis requires polysomnographic documentation of an increased number of PLMS in association with significant disruption of sleep architecture and symptomatology.
It is characterized by periodic episodes of repetitive and stereotyped limb movements that occur during sleep.
These movements can cause clinical sleep disturbance expressed by insomnia or excessive daytime sleepiness.

questions.explanation: PLMD is characterized by periodic episodes of repetitive and stereotyped limb movements that occur during sleep.

questions.question_text: Many patients with Chronic Fatigue Syndrome will meet the criteria for another psychiatric diagnosis, which is most commonly;
questions.explanation: There is a high rate of depression in patient with CFS.

questions.question_text: A 75 -year-old man with Parkinsons disease develops psychosis unrelated to levodopa use. Choose the best antipsychotic:
questions.explanation: In addition to the open -label studies, there have been two single -blind, randomized trials comparing quetiapine and clozapine.

questions.question_text: Which of the following factors have been implicated in the generation of periodic limb movement disorders?
questions.explanation: Dopaminergic impairment and iron deficiency have been implicated in the generation of PLMS.

questions.question_text: Mrs.Z has a history of bipolar depression and is on treatment with mood stabilizer throughout her pregnancy. She gave birth to a male child with Cleft palate. The most likely offending drug is;
questions.explanation: Data for Lamotrigine suggests a low risk of foetal malformation when used as monotherapy.

questions.question_text: The core symptom of neurasthenia is
questions.explanation: Chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS) is the current preferred name for a clinical syndrome whose central feature is severe fatigue.

questions.question_text: Mr. Q suffers from epilepsy and psychosis with paranoid delusions and auditory hallucination. He is worried about metabolic side effects of newer antipsychotics and would like to take an older antipsychotic medication. The drug that should be avoided in his case would be;
questions.explanation: Chlorpromazine is the most epileptogenic of the older drugs and ideally should be avoided completely.
